correctness.rationale: Summing the exact six compartment equations gives \(T'=b-\delta T\). At \(\xi=0\), summing the three noncompliant equations gives \(X'=(q(T-X)-(\nu+\delta))X\). At equality, with \(Y=T-K=Y_0e^{-\delta t}\), this is \(X'=q(Y-X)X\); the exact equation for \(1/X\) has an exponentially convergent integrating factor and yields \(tX\to1/q\) for every \(X_0>0\), including the explicit invariant slice \(X=X_0/(1+qX_0t)\) when \(T_0=K\). For \(R_D<1\), the infection subsystem is eventually dominated by a Hurwitz Metzler matrix, so infected classes decay exponentially; the recovered classes are stable linear equations with exponentially decaying forcing. The stated limits for \(S^*\) and \(K-S\) then follow from the exact population identities. For \(R_D>1\), the positive disease eigenvalue gives instability. The package verifier's rational example independently matches the zero behavioral eigenvalue, negative disease eigenvalues, and reciprocal solution, but the proof is analytic rather than experimental.

final_claim: At the exact behavioral threshold \(Kq/(\nu+\delta)=1\) with \(\xi=0\), every solution with positive initial noncompliant mass satisfies \(tX(t)\to1/q\).
